items.summary: Domain CX-10 claimed a band member who applies for a chair on their own band's post 'keeps review but loses decide'. The two owning features agree with each other and against it: 04.03.01 D-10 makes review and submission mutually exclusive (applicant-side, one-way) and 04.04.01 D-11 makes queue concealment total. CX-10 synthesis Q3/Q5 were rewritten to state the owned rule; the CX file already stated it correctly at CX-03 synthesis Q2, so this was one drifted location, not a second decision.
items.canonicalSource: 04.03-submission-audition/04.03.01-structured-submission.md:200 (D-10) — "**Review access and submission on the same post are mutually exclusive**, and the choice is applicant-side and one-way"; reinforced at :111 ("Applying revokes their review access on that post for its lifetime") and DT-09 at :157. AND 04.04-triage-shortlist-decisioning/04.04.01-review-queue-triage.md:218 (D-11) — "**A candidate can never triage — or see — a queue they are a candidate in.** The exclusion is automatic and **overrides any grant from 01**", with :121 "The queue is absent, not greyed out." Corroborated inside the drifted file itself at opportunities-casting-cx.md:126 — "Review/submit mutual exclusion (D-10) is enforced at 04.04.02."
items.fixApplied: opportunities-casting-cx.md, CX-10 only. (1) Synthesis Q3 rewritten: review access is entity-inherited and commit authority narrower, but neither survives becoming a candidate — D-10 cited as authoritative for the mutual exclusion and D-11 as authoritative on the queue side, with the queue absent rather than greyed out and the reason quoted from D-11 (a greyed-out card confirms who else applied). The 'keeps review but loses decide' clause is gone. (2) Synthesis Q5 rewritten: conversion to candidate and revocation of *review* access are one atomic act, not a narrowing of the decide right; the choice is put before the submission is sent (04.03.01:111 confirm string) and is one-way because a reversible revocation is not a control. (3) Relationship prose: DT-09 named as the widest form of the decider-cannot-be-candidate rule — 'what goes is the whole review seat, not only the vote'. (4) Role scoping line: 'the conflicted reviewer' → 'the member who must trade the review seat for the chair', since under D-10 they are not a reviewer once they apply. (5) CX-10 map row: relationship cell notes applying costs the review seat outright; evidence cell now cites 04.03.01 D-10 and 04.04.01 D-11 alongside DT-09 (7-column row preserved). No open question added — the tree already decided this twice; nothing is left unresolved.

items.summary: 04.02.01 D-06's auto-tombstone carried a 'stops accepting submissions' clause — a third, board-owned mechanism for closing a post, on top of the run-3-ratified decide-by (04.01.01 D-16) and the post's date. It contradicts three canonical statements AND D-06's own rationale sentence. The write-back half was struck; the presentation half (marker, sink, assumed-stale tombstone) is retained and sharpened, and the residual product question is tracked as a new Q-06 with an owner and a deferral target.
items.canonicalSource: 04.01-opportunity-posting-targeting/04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:208 (D-16) — "**The decide-by is what closes the post** (D-16)" and :209 — "**The date closes submission, the decide-by closes the post**"; :235 post-level lifecycle heading — "container; **status follows the slots**, never set directly" (D-08), enumerating Draft / Gate-blocked / Published / Reviewing / Decided / Submission closed / Closed / Withdrawn / Filled elsewhere and no stale or tombstoned state. AND opportunities-casting-cx.md:59-60 (CX-01 synthesis Q1) — "The post is owned by 04.01; 04.02 is a reader with no write-back ... it never mutates the post." Decisively, D-06's own Context column already said the narrower thing: "The board cannot make posters close their posts — that is 04.05.01's — but it can refuse to present an abandoned post as live."
items.thirdClosingMechanismCheck: Confirmed, and stated explicitly in the file. After the run-3 remediation that ratified 04.01.01 D-16, the post already carries exactly two closing dates — the post's date closes submission, the decide-by closes the post — plus the poster-driven terminals (withdrawn, filled elsewhere, all slots terminal). D-06's tombstone was a third, board-owned mechanism that stopped submissions on a clock nobody else reads: for a dep call the freshness interval is 48 h, so the tombstone fires at 96 h of poster inactivity while the decide-by is the event date three weeks out. The two rules disagreed by weeks on the domain's single most characteristic post type, and the board's clock measures poster *app activity*, not lateness. It is now scoped to presentation and cannot close anything.
items.fixApplied: 04.02.01-opportunity-board-search.md, five edits. (1) The D-06 prose block (:62-66): 'stops accepting submissions' replaced with 'the board **stops presenting it as live**', plus a new paragraph stating that the tombstone is presentation not lifecycle, quoting D-16 on both closing dates, D-08's 'follows the slots, never set directly' and the empty stale state, and CX-01 synthesis Q1's 'it never mutates the post'; it names the three-weeks-out dep call as the case that makes a board-side close indefensible and routes the remainder to Q-06. (2) D-06 decision row: title now reads 'auto-tombstone at 2x the type's interval — as presentation only. The tombstone never closes the post and never stops submissions'; Context column carries the reconciliation with citations (3-column row preserved). (3) New edge-case row 'User opens an assumed-stale listing' — still open, apply remains enabled, staleness stated rather than implied, D-13's response-reputation signal renders alongside (3-column row preserved). (4) Adjacent expiry edge-case row corrected to D-16's two dates: it read 'Closed — the date passed', which contradicts D-16 on briefs and open calls where the two dates are weeks apart; it now renders whichever transition landed. (5) Cross-cut notes to 04.01.01 and 04.05.01 amended — the 04.01.01 note gains an explicit one-way boundary ('D-06's assumed-stale tombstone is a rendering over that lifecycle, never a transition in it'), and the 04.05.01 rot note now says the auto-tombstone is load-bearing *as presentation*, so the rot stays in the data once it leaves the view.

trackedQuestionAdded.question: Should an abandoned post actually close, or only stop looking live? D-06's tombstone is presentation-only, so a post whose poster has vanished keeps accepting applications until its decide-by — 90 days on a member-wanted ad, months on a brief or open call — and every application landing in that window creates a disposition obligation (04.05.01 D-01) nobody will discharge. The board can detect abandonment and is the only surface that does; it cannot transition a post it does not own. If yes, the state belongs in 04.01.01's post-level lifecycle and the trigger with 04.05.01's obligation machinery — the board would render it, never cause it. If no, D-06 as now scoped is complete and the rot is contained to the view.
